1:
**Arma virumque cano, Troiae qui primus ab oris**

*arma* (n. acc. pl.) "arms, warfare"; *virum-que* (m. acc. sg.) "and the man" (acc. object of *cano*); *cano* (1st sg. pres. ind.) "I sing"; *Troiae* (f. gen. sg.) "of Troy"; *primus* (m. nom. sg.) "first"; *ab oris* (f. abl. pl.) "from the shores." The poet announces his dual theme—war and the hero who first came from Troy's coasts.
2:
**Italiam, fato profugus, Laviniaque venit**

*Italiam* (acc. sg., "Italy") – destination after *venit*; *fato* (abl. sg., "by fate") – ablative of cause; *profugus* (nom. sg. m., "exiled, fugitive") – predicative adjective describing the subject *qui*; *Laviniaque* (acc. pl. neut., "Lavinian [shores]") – *-que* coordinates with *litora* in the next line; *venit* (3rd sg. perf., "he came") – main verb. Aeneas, driven by destiny as an exile, reached Italy and the Lavinian coast.
3:
**litora, multum ille et terris iactatus et alto**

*litora* (n. acc. pl., "shores"); *multum* (adv., "much, greatly"); *iactatus* (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. m., "having been tossed/driven"); *terris* (f. abl. pl., "on/by lands"); *alto* (n. abl. sg., "on/by the deep/sea"). The hero, much tossed both on lands and on the sea, reaches the shores of Italy, with *iactatus* governing the ablatives of place where.
4: **vi** (abl. sing. of *vis*) "by the force/violence"; **superum** (gen. pl. of *superi*) "of the gods above"; **saevae** (gen. sing. fem. of *saevus*) "of savage/cruel"; **memorem** (acc. sing. fem. of *memor*) "remembering/mindful"; **Iunonis** (gen. sing. of *Iuno*) "of Juno"; **iram** (acc. sing. of *ira*) "wrath/anger." The hero was tossed about by the violence of the gods above, on account of the wrath of savage Juno who remembered (her grievances).
5:
**multa** (acc. pl. neut., "many things") **quoque** ("also") **et** ("and") **bello** (abl. sg., "in/by war") **passus** (perf. part., "having suffered") **dum** ("while") **conderet** (imperf. subj., "he might found") **urbem** (acc. sg., "city").

Aeneas suffered many things also in war while he was founding his city. The subjunctive *conderet* with *dum* expresses contemporaneous action with the main verb *passus [est]*.
6:
**inferretque deos Latio, genus unde Latinum,**

*inferretque*: 3rd sg. impf. subj. act. of *inferre*, "and he might bring in/introduce"; *deos*: acc. pl. m., "the gods" (his household gods/Penates); *Latio*: dat. sg. of *Latium*, "into Latium"; *genus*: nom. sg. n., "the race/lineage"; *unde*: relative adv., "from which/whence"; *Latinum*: nom. sg. n. of *Latinus*, "Latin." Aeneas would bring his gods to Latium, from which the Latin race and Alban fathers would descend.
7:
**Albanique patres, atque altae moenia Romae.**

*Albanique* (adj., nom. pl. masc., "Alban") modifies *patres* (noun, nom. pl., "fathers/senators"); *atque* (conj., "and") connects the two objects; *altae* (adj., gen. sg. fem., "lofty/high") modifies *Romae* (noun, gen. sg., "of Rome"); *moenia* (noun, nom./acc. pl. neut., "walls/fortifications"). This line completes the genealogical sequence from Troy to Rome, naming the Alban fathers (descendants of Aeneas through his son Ascanius who founded Alba Longa) and culminating in Rome's mighty walls as the destined outcome of Aeneas's journey.
8:
**Musa, mihi causas memora, quo numine laeso**

*Musa* (nom. sg., "Muse") is invoked in the imperative *memora* ("recall, recount"). *mihi* (dat. sg., "to me") indicates the indirect object. *causas* (acc. pl., "causes, reasons") is the direct object. *quo numine laeso* (abl. sg., "with what divinity offended/wounded") expresses attendant circumstances, with *laeso* as a perfect passive participle modifying *numine*.
9:
**quidve dolens, regina deum tot volvere casus**

*quidve* (conjunction, "or what") connects alternative questions about divine motivation; *dolens* (present participle, nominative singular, "grieving") modifies *regina*; *regina deum* (nominative + genitive plural, "queen of the gods") refers to Juno; *volvere* (present active infinitive, "to roll/cause to revolve") governs *casus*; *tot casus* (accusative plural, "so many misfortunes") are the object of *volvere*. The line asks why Juno, grieving, compelled a pious hero to endure such repeated calamities.
10:
**insignem pietate virum, tot adire labores**

*insignem* (acc. sg. m., adj. from *insignis*) = "distinguished, remarkable," modifying *virum*. *pietate* (abl. sg. f., noun from *pietas*) = "piety, devotion," ablative of respect. *virum* (acc. sg. m., noun from *vir*) = "man," object of *impulerit*. *tot* (indecl. adj.) = "so many," modifying *labores*. *adire* (pres. inf., verb from *adeo*) = "to undergo, approach," complementary infinitive with *impulerit*. *labores* (acc. pl. m., noun from *labor*) = "labors, hardships," object of *adire*. 

The line questions why Juno compelled a man distinguished for his piety to undergo so many
11: **impulerit** (perf. subj. act., 3rd sg. of *impello*) "drove" or "compelled"; **tantaene** (nom. pl. fem., interrogative adj. with enclitic *-ne*) "so great?"; **animis** (dat. pl. of *animus*) "in the minds/hearts"; **caelestibus** (dat. pl. of *caelestis*) "of the heavenly ones" or "celestial"; **irae** (nom. pl. of *ira*) "angers" or "wraths." The poet asks rhetorically what drove the goddess to inflict such suffering on pious Aeneas, questioning whether such great wraths exist in the hearts of the gods.
12: **Urbs** (nom. sg. f.) "city"; **antiqua** (nom. sg. f. adj.) "ancient"; **fuit** (3rd sg. perf. act. ind. of *sum*) "was/there was"; **Tyrii** (nom. pl. m. adj.) "Tyrian"; **tenuere** (3rd pl. perf. act. ind. of *teneo*, syncopated form of *tenuerunt*) "held/occupied"; **coloni** (nom. pl. m.) "colonists/settlers." The line introduces Carthage as an ancient city held by Tyrian colonists, beginning Juno's backstory and her hostility toward the Trojans.
13: **Karthago** (nom. sg., f.): Carthage, the ancient Phoenician city in North Africa. **Italiam** (acc. sg., f.): Italy, object of *contra*. **contra** (prep. + acc.): opposite to, facing. **Tiberina** (acc. pl., n.): Tiber-related things, here the mouths of the Tiber River. **longe** (adv.): far, at a distance. Carthage stood far opposite Italy and the Tiber's mouths.
14: **ostia** (n. pl. acc.) "mouths" or "harbors" – the outlets of the Tiber river; **dives** (adj. nom. f. sg.) "rich"; **opum** (gen. pl. of *opes*) "in resources/wealth"; **studiis** (abl. pl.) "in pursuits/zeal"; **asperrima** (superl. adj. nom. f. sg.) "most fierce/savage"; **belli** (gen. sg.) "of war." Carthage stands geographically opposite Italy and the Tiber's mouths, rich in resources and supremely fierce in its warlike pursuits.
15: **quam** (relative pronoun, acc. sing. fem.) "which" refers to Carthage; **Iuno** (nom. sing.) "Juno"; **fertur** (3rd sing. pres. pass. indic. of *fero*) "is said/reported"; **magis** (adv.) "more"; **omnibus** (abl. pl. neut. with *terris*) "all." Juno is reported to have cherished this one city more than all other lands, with *posthabita...Samo* (abl. absolute) indicating "even Samos having been placed second."
16:
**posthabita coluisse Samo; hic illius arma,**

*posthabita* (perfect passive participle, ablative singular feminine from *posthabeo*) "having been set aside/postponed," modifies *Samo*; *coluisse* (perfect active infinitive from *colo*) "to have cherished/cultivated," dependent on *fertur* from the previous line; *Samo* (ablative singular) "than Samos," ablative of comparison with *posthabita*; *arma* (nominative/accusative plural neuter) "arms/weapons." Juno cherished Carthage more than even Samos (her birthplace now set aside in favor); here were her arms/weapons.
17:
**Target line: hic currus fuit; hoc regnum dea gentibus esse,**

*hic* (adverb) = here; *currus* (nom. sg. m.) = chariot; *fuit* (3rd sg. perf. act. indic. of *sum*) = was; *hoc* (acc. sg. n. demonstrative) = this; *regnum* (acc. sg. n.) = kingdom/dominion; *gentibus* (dat. pl. f.) = for the nations/peoples; *esse* (pres. act. infin. of *sum*) = to be. 

Juno's chariot was here (at Carthage); the goddess strives that this place be the ruling power over the nations, with *hoc regnum esse* as indirect statement dependent on *tendit* in the following line.
18:
**si qua fata sinant, iam tum tenditque fovetque.**

Key words: *si* (conj.) "if"; *fata* (n. nom./acc. pl., "fates") subject of *sinant*; *sinant* (pres. subj. 3rd pl. *sino*) "should allow/permit"; *tendit* (pres. indic. 3rd sg. *tendo*) "strives for, works toward"; *fovet* (pres. indic. 3rd sg. *foveo*) "cherishes, fosters." Juno already then (referring to Carthage's future supremacy) strives for and cherishes this destiny, if only the fates should permit it.
19:
**Progeniem sed enim Troiano a sanguine duci**

*Progeniem* (acc. sing., "offspring/race") is the object of *audierat* (from the next line); *Troiano...a sanguine* (abl. of source with preposition, "from Trojan blood") indicates origin; *duci* (pres. pass. inf., "to be led/descended") completes the indirect statement. Juno had heard that a race descended from Trojan blood would one day overthrow the Tyrian citadels. *Sed enim* provides emphatic transition ("but indeed/for").
20:
**audierat, Tyrias olim quae verteret arces;**

*audierat* (pluperfect active indicative, 3rd sg. of *audio*) = "she had heard"; *Tyrias* (accusative plural feminine adjective modifying *arces*) = "Tyrian"; *olim* (adverb) = "one day, someday"; *quae* (nominative singular feminine relative pronoun, subject of *verteret*) = "which" (referring to *progeniem*); *verteret* (imperfect subjunctive, 3rd sg. of *verto*) = "would overthrow"; *arces* (accusative plural of *arx*) = "citadels, strongholds." Juno had heard that a Trojan-descended race would one day destroy the Tyrian citadels (i.e., Carthage in the Punic Wars).
21:
**hinc** (adv., "from this source/hence") **populum** (acc. sing. m., "a people/nation") **late** (adv., "widely") **regem** (acc. sing. m., "ruling") **belloque** (abl. sing. n., "and in war") **superbum** (acc. sing. m., "proud/mighty"). 

Juno had heard that a people ruling widely and proud in war would come from this Trojan source to destroy her beloved Carthage; *populum* is the object of *venturum* (in the next line), with *regem* and *superbum* as predicative adjectives describing Rome's future dominance.
22: **venturum** (acc. sg. m. fut. act. participle of *venio*) "about to come"; **excidio** (dat. sg. of *excidium*) "for/to the destruction"; **Libyae** (gen. or dat. sg. of *Libya*) "of/to Libya"; **volvere** (pres. act. inf. of *volvo*) "to roll, unroll, ordain"; **Parcas** (acc. pl. of *Parca*) "the Fates." Juno fears that this people (the Romans) will come for the destruction of Libya (Carthage), as the Fates were spinning/decreeing it.
23:
**Id metuens, veterisque memor Saturnia belli,**

*Id* (demonstrative pronoun, neuter accusative singular) = "that," object of *metuens*; *metuens* (present participle of *metuo*, nominative singular) = "fearing"; *veteris* (adjective, genitive singular) = "old, former," modifying *belli*; *memor* (adjective + genitive) = "mindful of, remembering"; *Saturnia* (adjective/epithet, nominative singular) = "daughter of Saturn," i.e., Juno; *belli* (noun, genitive singular) = "of the war," referring to the Trojan War. Juno, fearing this prophesied destruction of Carthage and remembering her old warfare at Troy, prepares her opposition to the Trojans.
24:
**prima quod ad Troiam pro caris gesserat Argis—**

*prima* (nom. sg. fem., "first" or "foremost," modifying Saturnia): Juno as the principal actor. *quod* (conjunction, "because"): introduces a causal clause explaining her hostility. *gesserat* (pluperfect active, 3rd sg., from *gero*, "to wage/conduct"): she had waged. *pro caris...Argis* (preposition + abl., "on behalf of dear/beloved Argos"): for Greece in the Trojan War. The line recalls Juno's partisan role supporting the Greeks against Troy.
25:
**necdum etiam causae irarum saevique dolores**

*necdum* (adv.) = "not yet"; *causae* (nom. pl., f.) = "causes"; *irarum* (gen. pl., f.) = "of her anger/wrath"; *saevi* (gen. sg., m./n. or nom. pl., m.) = "of cruel/savage" (modifying *dolores*); *dolores* (nom. pl., m.) = "griefs, resentments." The line continues the explanation of Juno's hostility: not yet had the causes of her anger and cruel grievances departed from her mind.
26: **exciderant** (pluperfect active indicative, 3rd pl. of *excido*) "had fallen out/away," **animo** (ablative of separation) "from [her] mind," **manet** (present active indicative, 3rd sg. of *maneo*) "remains," **alta mente repostum** (ablative of place where + neuter nominative/accusative sg. perfect passive participle of *repono*) "stored deep in [her] mind." The causes of Juno's anger had not yet fallen from her mind; the judgment remains deeply stored within her.
27:
**iudicium Paridis spretaeque iniuria formae**

*iudicium* (nom. n. sg., "judgment") refers to Paris's award of the golden apple; *Paridis* (gen. m. sg., "of Paris") possessive genitive; *spretae* (gen. f. sg., perf. pass. partic. of *sperno*, "scorned/rejected") modifies *formae*; *iniuria* (nom. f. sg., "insult/injury"); *formae* (gen. f. sg., "of beauty") objective genitive. Juno recalls Paris's judgment that spurned her beauty in favor of Venus, a lasting source of divine wrath.
28:
**et genus invisum, et rapti Ganymedis honores.**

*genus* (n. nom./acc. sg.): "race, offspring" (referring to the Trojan people); *invisum* (adj. nom./acc. sg. n.): "hated"; *rapti* (perf. pass. part. gen. sg. m.): "seized, abducted"; *Ganymedis* (m. gen. sg.): "of Ganymede" (Trojan youth abducted by Jupiter to be cupbearer); *honores* (m. nom./acc. pl.): "honors, privileges." Juno's rage is further inflamed by her hatred of the Trojan race and her resentment over the honors given to the abducted Ganymede, who supplanted Juno's daughter Hebe as cupbearer to the gods.
29:
**His accensa super, iactatos aequore toto**

*His* (ablative plural, demonstrative pronoun) "by these things"; *accensa* (nominative feminine singular, perfect passive participle of *accendo*) "inflamed, enraged"; *super* (adverb) "in addition, moreover"; *iactatos* (accusative masculine plural, perfect passive participle of *iacto*) "storm-tossed, harried"; *aequore* (ablative singular of *aequor*) "over/on the sea"; *toto* (ablative singular of *totus*) "all, whole." Juno, inflamed moreover by these grievances, drove the Trojans who had been tossed over the entire sea.
30:
**Troas, reliquias Danaum atque immitis Achilli,**

*Troas* (acc. pl. m., "Trojans") is the direct object continued from the previous line's *arcebat*. *reliquias* (acc. pl. f., "remnants, survivors") stands in apposition to *Troas*. *Danaum* (gen. pl. m., "of the Greeks") is an objective genitive with *reliquias*. *immitis* (gen. sg. m./f., "pitiless, cruel") modifies *Achilli* (gen. sg. m., "of Achilles"), both dependent on *reliquias*—the Trojans are survivors of both the Greeks generally and savage Achilles specifically.
31:
**arcebat longe Latio, multosque per annos**

*arcebat* (imperfect active, 3rd sg. of *arceo*) "was keeping away"; *longe* (adverb) "far"; *Latio* (ablative of separation with *Latium*) "from Latium"; *multosque* (accusative plural masculine of *multus*) "and for many"; *annos* (accusative plural of *annus*) "years." Juno was keeping the Trojans far from Latium for many years as they wandered the seas driven by fate.
32:
**errabant, acti fatis, maria omnia circum.**

*errabant* (3rd pl. imperf. act. indic. of *erro*, "they were wandering"); *acti* (perf. pass. part. nom. pl. m. of *ago*, "driven"); *fatis* (abl. pl. of *fatum*, "by the fates"); *maria omnia* (acc. pl. neut., "all the seas"); *circum* (adv./prep., "around"). The Trojans wandered all the seas around, driven by the fates—emphasizing their prolonged suffering and divine compulsion before founding Rome.
33: **Tantae** (gen. sg. f. adj., modifying *molis*) "of such great"; **molis** (gen. sg. f. noun, predicate genitive) "effort, toil, massive undertaking"; **erat** (3rd sg. imperf. act. ind., *sum*) "it was"; **Romanam** (acc. sg. f. adj., modifying *gentem*) "Roman"; **condere** (pres. act. inf., *condo*) "to found, establish"; **gentem** (acc. sg. f. noun) "race, nation." This famous editorial intrusion declares the immense difficulty required to found the Roman people, employing a genitive of quality construction with the impersonal verb.
34: **Vix** (adverb): "scarcely," "barely." **conspectu** (masculine noun, ablative singular of *conspectus*): "sight," "view." **Siculae** (adjective, genitive singular feminine, modifying *telluris*): "Sicilian." **telluris** (feminine noun, genitive singular of *tellus*): "land," "earth." **altum** (neuter noun, accusative singular of *altum*): "the deep (sea)," "the open waters." The Trojans had barely sailed out of sight of Sicilian land into the deep sea when Juno's intervention begins.
35:
**vela dabant laeti, et spumas salis aere ruebant,**

*vela* (n. acc. pl., "sails") *dabant* (imperf. act. ind., "were setting/giving") *laeti* (adj. nom. pl. m., "joyful") *spumas* (n. acc. pl., "foam") *salis* (n. gen. sg., "of salt/sea") *aere* (n. abl. sg., "with bronze," i.e., bronze-fitted prows) *ruebant* (imperf. act. ind., "were plowing/churning"). The Trojans joyfully set sail from Sicily, their bronze-beaked ships churning the sea's foam, just before Juno's intervention.
36:
**cum Iuno, aeternum servans sub pectore volnus,**

*cum* (conjunction) "when"; *Iuno* (nom. sg.) "Juno" (subject); *aeternum* (acc. sg. neut. adj.) "eternal," modifying *volnus*; *servans* (pres. part. nom. sg.) "keeping, preserving"; *sub pectore* (abl. of place) "beneath her breast, in her heart"; *volnus* (acc. sg. neut.) "wound." The goddess nurses an undying grievance as she observes the Trojans' progress.
37: **Mene** (acc. pronoun, "me") **incepto** (abl. neut. sing., "from my undertaking/purpose") **desistere** (pres. inf., "to cease/desist") **victam** (acc. fem. sing. perf. pass. part., "conquered/defeated") **haec secum** (acc. neut. pl. pron. + reflex. abl., "these things with herself"). Juno deliberates indignantly whether she, defeated, should abandon her enterprise; *haec secum* introduces her internal monologue, and the -ne enclitic marks the rhetorical question.
38:
**Target line:** *nec posse Italia Teucrorum avertere regem?*

**Key words:** *nec* (negative conjunction, "nor/and not"); *posse* (present infinitive of possum, "to be able"); *Italia* (ablative of separation, "from Italy"); *Teucrorum* (genitive plural, "of the Trojans"); *avertere* (present infinitive, "to turn away/repel"); *regem* (accusative singular, "the king").

Juno protests that she cannot prevent the Trojan king from reaching Italy, questioning why Pallas could destroy the Greek fleet but she is forbidden by the fates to act similarly.
39:
**Quippe vetor fatis. Pallasne exurere classem**

*quippe* (adv.) = "indeed, forsooth" (ironic); *vetor* (1st sg. pres. pass. indic., *veto*) = "I am forbidden"; *fatis* (abl. pl., *fatum*) = "by the fates"; *Pallas* (nom. sg.) = "Pallas (Athena)"; *exurere* (pres. act. inf., *exuro*) = "to burn up"; *classem* (acc. sg., *classis*) = "fleet." Juno protests bitterly that she is constrained by fate, while Pallas was permitted to incinerate the Greek fleet (for Ajax's sacrilege).
40: **Argivum** (adj. acc. masc. sing.) "Greek/Argive," modifying *classem* from the previous line; **ipsos** (intensive pron. acc. masc. plur.) "themselves," referring to the Greek warriors; **potuit** (perf. 3rd sing. of *possum*) "was able"; **submergere** (pres. act. inf. of *submergo*) "to sink, submerge"; **ponto** (abl. masc. sing. of *pontus*) "in/by the sea." Juno indignantly recalls that Pallas Athena could both burn the Greek fleet and drown the warriors themselves in the sea for the crime of one man, Ajax Oileus.
41: **unius** (adj., gen. sg., "of one") **ob** (prep. + acc., "on account of") **noxam** (noun, acc. sg., "crime, offense") **furias** (noun, acc. pl., "mad rage, frenzy") **Aiacis Oilei** (proper nouns, gen. sg., "of Ajax, son of Oileus"). Juno protests that she could destroy the entire Greek fleet on account of one man's crime and the mad violence of Ajax the Lesser (who raped Cassandra at Athena's altar).
42:
**Ipsa, Iovis rapidum iaculata e nubibus ignem,**

*Ipsa* (intensive pronoun, nom. sing. fem.): "she herself" (Juno, emphatic subject). *Iovis* (noun, gen. sing.): "of Jove/Jupiter" (possessive, modifying *ignem*). *rapidum* (adj., acc. sing. masc.): "swift, snatching" (modifying *ignem*). *iaculata* (perfect participle, nom. sing. fem.): "having hurled" (from *iaculor*, describing Juno's action). *nubibus* (noun, abl. plur.): "from the clouds" (ablative of separation with *e*). *ignem* (noun, acc. sing. masc.): "thunderbolt, fire" (direct object of *iaculata*). 

Juno herself
43:
**disiecitque rates evertitque aequora ventis**

*disiecit* (perf. ind. act. 3rd sg. of *disicio*) "scattered"; *rates* (acc. pl. f.) "ships, rafts"; *evertit* (perf. ind. act. 3rd sg. of *everto*) "overturned, upheaved"; *aequora* (acc. pl. n.) "seas, waters"; *ventis* (abl. pl. m.) "with/by winds." Juno (continuing from *ipsa*) both scattered the ships and churned up the seas with storm winds, intensifying the destruction wrought by her thunderbolt.
44:
**illum** (acc. sg. m. of *ille*) "that one" / "him" – direct object of *corripuit* (from the next line), referring to a specific Greek warrior. **expirantem** (pres. part. acc. sg. m. of *exspiro*) "breathing out" – modifying *illum*. **transfixo pectore** (abl. sg. n. of *transfigo* + *pectus*) "with pierced chest" – ablative absolute. **flammas** (acc. pl. f. of *flamma*) "flames" – direct object of *expirantem*. 

The line depicts a warrior breathing out flames from his pierced chest, creating a vivid image of destruction during the storm or battle scene.
45: **turbine** (abl. sing., m., "whirlwind, storm") **corripuit** (3rd sing. perf. act., "seized, snatched up") **scopuloque** (abl. sing., m., "cliff, rock") **infixit** (3rd sing. perf. act., "fastened, impaled") **acuto** (abl. sing., m., "sharp, pointed"). Juno recounts how she seized Aeneas's ship in a whirlwind and dashed it upon a sharp crag, expressing her vengeful power against the Trojans.
46:
**Ast ego, quae divom incedo regina, Iovisque**

*Ast* (conjunction, "but"); *ego* (nominative pronoun, "I"); *quae* (nominative relative pronoun, "who"); *divom* (archaic genitive plural of *dī*, "of the gods"); *incedo* (1st sg. present indicative, "I walk/proceed"); *regina* (nominative, "queen"); *Iovisque* (*Iovis* genitive + *-que*, "and of Jupiter"). Juno bitterly contrasts her divine status as queen of the gods and Jupiter's consort with her inability to prevent Aeneas's success.
47:
**et soror et coniunx, una cum gente tot annos**

Key words: *soror* (nom. sg. f., "sister"), *coniunx* (nom. sg. f., "wife/spouse"), *una* (adv., "together"), *gente* (abl. sg. f., "race/people"), *annos* (acc. pl. m., "years"). Juno identifies herself emphatically as both sister and wife of Jupiter, expressing her prolonged struggle against a single people (the Trojans) for so many years.
48:
**bella gero! Et quisquam numen Iunonis adoret**

*bella* (n. acc. pl. of *bellum*) "wars"; *gero* (1st sg. pres. indic. of *gerere*) "I wage"; *quisquam* (nom. sg. indef. pron.) "anyone"; *numen* (n. acc. sg. of *numen*) "divinity, divine power"; *Iunonis* (gen. sg. of *Iuno*) "of Juno"; *adoret* (3rd sg. pres. subj. of *adorare*) "worship, adore." Juno bitterly asks whether anyone will still worship her divine power after she wages wars (yet fails to prevent Trojan success).
49: **praeterea** (adv.) "hereafter, in the future"; **supplex** (adj., nom. sg.) "suppliant, as a suppliant"; **aris** (n., dat./abl. pl. of *ara*) "on/to the altars"; **imponet** (v., fut. 3rd sg. of *imponere*) "will place"; **honorem** (n., acc. sg. of *honor*) "honor, offering." Juno asks rhetorically whether any mortal will still worship her by placing votive offerings on her altars as a suppliant, given her apparent impotence to prevent the Trojans' success.
50:
**Talia flammato secum dea corde volutans**

*Talia* (neut. pl. acc., "such things") is the object of *volutans* (pres. part. nom. sg. fem., "turning over, pondering"), describing *dea* (nom. sg. fem., "goddess," i.e., Juno). *Flammato...corde* (abl. sg. neut., "with inflamed heart") is an ablative of means/manner, depicting her emotional state. *Secum* ("with herself, within herself") emphasizes her internal deliberation. Juno broods over these grievances with burning rage before journeying to Aeolus's storm-realm.
51: **nimborum** (gen. pl., "of storm-clouds") **in patriam** (acc. sg., "into the fatherland/homeland") **loca** (acc. pl., "places") **feta** (acc. pl. neuter, perf. part. of *feto*, "teeming/pregnant with") **furentibus austris** (abl. pl., "with raging south winds"). Juno arrives at Aeolia, the homeland of storm-clouds, a region teeming with wild southern gales under Aeolus' control.
52: **Aeoliam** (adj. acc. sg. f., "Aeolian") modifies an understood *terram*; **venit** (3rd sg. pres./perf. indic., "comes/came"); **Hic** (adv., "here"); **vasto** (adj. abl. sg. n., "vast") modifies **antro** (abl. sg., "in a cave"); **rex** (nom. sg., "king") **Aeolus** (nom. sg., proper name). Aeneas arrives at Aeolia, where King Aeolus rules from his enormous cavern.
53:
**luctantes ventos tempestatesque sonoras**

*luctantes* (pres. act. participle, acc. masc. pl. from *luctor*) "struggling"; *ventos* (acc. masc. pl. of *ventus*) "winds"; *tempestatesque* (*-que* enclitic "and" + acc. fem. pl. of *tempestas*) "storms"; *sonoras* (acc. fem. pl. of *sonorus, -a, -um*) "roaring, thunderous." Aeolus controls the struggling winds and roaring storms within his vast cave through his power and restraints.
54: **imperio** (n., abl. sing.) "by command/authority"; **premit** (3rd sing. pres. act. indic. of *premo*) "presses down, restrains"; **vinclis** (n., abl. pl.) "with chains/bonds"; **carcere** (n., abl. sing.) "with prison/confinement"; **frenat** (3rd sing. pres. act. indic. of *freno*) "bridles, curbs." Aeolus restrains the struggling winds by his sovereign command, binding them with chains and confining them in their prison-cave.
55:
**Illi indignantes magno cum murmure montis**

*Illi* (nom. pl. masc., "those [winds]"), *indignantes* (pres. part. nom. pl., "raging/chafing indignantly"), *magno* (abl. sg. neut., "with great"), *murmure* (abl. sg., "roar/rumbling"), *montis* (gen. sg., "of the mountain"). The imprisoned winds rage indignantly with a great roar within the mountain, their fury contained by Aeolus's barriers.
56:
**circum claustra fremunt; celsa sedet Aeolus arce**

*circum* (prep. + acc.): around; *claustra* (n. acc. pl.): barriers, enclosures; *fremunt* (3rd pl. pres. indic.): they roar, rage; *celsa* (abl. fem. sg.): on/in the lofty; *arce* (abl. fem. sg.): citadel, height. The winds roar around their prison while Aeolus sits enthroned on his high citadel, controlling them before he soothes their fury.
57: **sceptra** (n. acc. pl., "scepter") **tenens** (pres. part. nom. sg., "holding"), **mollitque** (verb 3rd sg. pres., "and softens"), **animos** (m. acc. pl., "spirits/tempers"), **temperat** (verb 3rd sg. pres., "restrains/moderates"), **iras** (f. acc. pl., "angers/rages"). Aeolus sits in his lofty citadel holding his scepter of authority, soothing the spirits of the winds and controlling their violent rages.
58:
**Ni faciat, maria ac terras caelumque profundum**

*Ni* (conjunction, "if not, unless") introduces a contrary-to-fact condition; *faciat* (3rd sg. pres. subj. of *facio*, "he does/makes") continues the subjunctive construction; *maria* (nom./acc. pl. neut. of *mare*, "seas"), *terras* (acc. pl. fem. of *terra*, "lands"), and *caelum* (acc. sg. neut. of *caelum*, "sky/heaven") with *profundum* (acc. sg. neut. adj., "deep, profound") form a cosmic triad of objects.
59:
**quippe** (adverb): "indeed," "for certainly" – causal/explanatory particle justifying the preceding statement.

**ferant** (verb, 3rd pl. pres. subj., *fero*): "they would carry" – potential subjunctive expressing what the winds would do.

**rapidi** (adj., nom. pl. masc., *rapidus*): "rushing," "violent" – modifies the implied subject (winds).

**secum** (prep. + pron.): "with themselves" – *se* + *cum*, indicating what they sweep along together.

**verrant** (verb, 3rd pl. pres. subj., *verro*): "sweep away," "brush along" – paired with *ferant* to describe the destructive force of the unleashed winds through the air (*per auras*).
60:
**Sed pater omnipotens speluncis abdidit atris**

*pater* (nom. sg. m.): "father" (i.e., Jupiter); *omnipotens* (nom. sg. m.): "all-powerful," "almighty"; *speluncis* (abl. pl. f.): "in caves"; *abdidit* (perf. 3rd sg.): "hid," "concealed" (from *abdo*); *atris* (abl. pl. f.): "dark," "black." Jupiter, fearing the destructive power of the winds, concealed them in dark caverns.
61:
**hoc metuens, molemque et montis insuper altos**

*hoc* (neuter accusative singular, demonstrative pronoun): "this," object of *metuens*. *metuens* (present active participle, nominative singular from *metuo*): "fearing." *molemque* (feminine accusative singular noun with enclitic *-que*): "mass" or "massive structure," coordinated object. *montis* (masculine accusative plural noun): "mountains." *insuper* (adverb): "on top," "above." *altos* (masculine accusative plural adjective): "high," modifying *montis*. Jupiter, fearing this threat, imprisoned the winds beneath a massive barrier and high mountains piled on top.
62:
**imposuit**: perfect active indicative, 3rd singular of *impono*, "he placed (upon)" or "imposed."
**regemque**: accusative singular of *rex*, coordinated with *molem*, "and a king."
**dedit**: perfect active indicative, 3rd singular of *do*, "he gave."
**foedere certo**: ablative of means, *foedus* with *certus*, "by/under a fixed compact" or "by a sure covenant."

Jupiter imposed (the mass and mountains) and gave a king who would know, under fixed terms, to restrain and to slacken the reins.
63: **premere** (infinitive, "to restrain/press"), **laxas** (acc. pl. fem. adj., "loose/slack"), **sciret** (impf. subj., "would know how"), **habenas** (acc. pl. fem., "reins"). Jupiter appointed a king who would know how to tighten control and slacken the reins as commanded, governing under fixed treaty terms.
64:
**Ad quem tum Iuno supplex his vocibus usa est:**

*Ad quem* (preposition + accusative relative pronoun) "to whom"; *Iuno* (nominative singular) "Juno," subject; *supplex* (nominative singular adjective) "suppliant, as a suppliant"; *vocibus* (ablative plural, *vox*) "with words/speech"; *usa est* (perfect deponent, *utor* + ablative) "used, employed." Juno approaches Aeolus in the posture of a supplicant, employing carefully chosen words to secure his aid.
65: **Aeole**: vocative singular, addressing Aeolus, god of the winds. **tibi**: dative singular of *tu*, "to you." **divom**: archaic genitive plural of *deus* (= *deorum*), "of the gods." **pater**: nominative singular, "father," in apposition to *rex*. **rex**: nominative singular, "king," subject of an implied verb; together with *pater*, this phrase refers to Jupiter, who grants authority to Aeolus.
66:
**Target line:** *et mulcere dedit fluctus et tollere vento*

**Gloss:** *mulcere* (pres. act. inf., "to calm/soothe") and *tollere* (pres. act. inf., "to raise/lift") are complementary infinitives dependent on *dedit* (perf. act. ind. 3rd sg. of *do*, "he gave/granted"). *fluctus* (acc. pl. m., "waves") is the object of both infinitives, while *vento* (abl. sg. m., "by/with wind") is ablative of means. Jupiter has granted Aeolus the power both to calm the waves and to raise them by means of wind.
67:
**gens inimica mihi Tyrrhenum navigat aequor**

*gens* (nom. sg. f.) "race, people"; *inimica* (nom. sg. f. adj.) "hostile" (with dat. *mihi* "to me"); *Tyrrhenum* (acc. sg. n. adj.) "Tyrrhenian, Etruscan"; *navigat* (3rd sg. pres. act. ind.) "sails across"; *aequor* (acc. sg. n.) "sea, plain of water." 

Juno complains that a race hostile to her is sailing the Tyrrhenian Sea (between Italy and Sicily), carrying Troy's conquered gods to Italy.
68:
**Ilium** (acc. sg., neut.) "Troy" – **in** + **Italiam** (acc. sg., fem.) "into Italy" – **portans** (pres. part., nom. sg.) "carrying" – **victos** (perf. pass. part., acc. pl., masc.) "conquered" – **Penates** (acc. pl., masc.) "household gods."

Juno describes Aeneas bearing Troy and its defeated Penates toward Italy, emphasizing the persistence of the conquered Trojan legacy that she seeks to destroy.
69:
**incute vim ventis submersasque obrue puppes**

*incute* (imperat. act., "hurl, drive") – Juno commands Aeolus to unleash force; *vim* (acc. sing., "force, violence") – object of *incute*; *ventis* (dat./abl. pl., "winds") – indirect object or instrument; *submersas* (perf. part. pass. acc. pl. fem., "submerged") modifies *puppes*; *obrue* (imperat. act., "overwhelm, bury") – second command; *puppes* (acc. pl. fem., "ships, sterns") – object of *obrue*. Juno urges violent destruction of the Trojan fleet through storm and shipwreck.
70:
**Target line:** *aut age diversos et disiice corpora ponto.*

**Key words:** *age* (2nd sg. pres. imper. of *ago*) = "drive"; *diversos* (acc. pl. masc. adj.) = "in different directions, scattered"; *disiice* (2nd sg. pres. imper. of *disicio*) = "scatter, disperse"; *corpora* (acc. pl. neut. noun) = "bodies"; *ponto* (abl. sg. masc. of *pontus*) = "over/on the sea."

Juno commands Aeolus either to drive the Trojans apart in different directions and scatter their bodies across the sea, intensifying her demand for their destruction.
71: **Sunt** (3rd pl. pres. ind. of *sum*) "there are"; **mihi** (dat. sg. of *ego*) "to me, I have"; **bis septem** "twice seven, fourteen"; **praestanti** (abl. sg. of *praestans, praestantis*, pres. part. of *praesto*) "excelling, outstanding"; **corpore** (abl. sg. of *corpus, corporis*, n.) "in body, in beauty"; **nymphae** (nom. pl. of *nympha*, f.) "nymphs." Juno offers Aeolus fourteen nymphs of surpassing beauty as a bribe to unleash the winds against Aeneas's fleet.
72:
**quarum quae forma pulcherrima Deiopea**

*quarum* (gen. pl. fem. of *qui, quae, quod*): "of whom," referring back to the nymphs. *quae* (nom. sg. fem. relative pronoun): "who," introducing the relative clause identifying Deiopea. *forma* (abl. sg. of *forma, -ae* f.): "in beauty/form," ablative of respect. *pulcherrima* (nom. sg. fem. superlative of *pulcher*): "most beautiful." *Deiopea* (nom. sg., Greek name): the nymph Deiopeia, subject of the clause. Juno specifies which nymph is fairest among the fourteen she possesses.
73: **conubio** (noun, dative/ablative singular, "in marriage") **iungam** (verb, 1st sing. future, "I shall join") **stabili** (adjective, dative/ablative singular, "lasting, permanent") **propriam** (adjective, accusative singular feminine, "as your own") **dicabo** (verb, 1st sing. future, "I shall dedicate/assign"). Juno promises to unite Deiopea to Aeolus in permanent wedlock and assign her as his own possession.
74:
**omnis ut tecum meritis pro talibus annos**

*omnis* (acc. pl. m./f., modifying *annos*) "all"; *tecum* (prep. + abl.) "with you"; *meritis* (abl. pl. n., from *meritum*) "for services/deserts"; *pro* (prep. + abl.) "in return for"; *talibus* (abl. pl. n./m./f., from *talis*) "such (great)"; *annos* (acc. pl. m., from *annus*) "years." Dido promises that her consort may spend all his years with her in exchange for such great services.
75: **exigat** (pres. subj., 3rd sg. of *exigo*) "may he pass/spend"; **pulchra** (abl. sg. fem. of *pulcher*) "beautiful," modifying *prole*; **prole** (abl. sg. of *proles*) "offspring/children"; **parentem** (acc. sg. of *parens*) "parent," in apposition to *te*. Juno wishes that the hero may pass all his years with her and that she may make him a parent through beautiful offspring, expressing a blessing of prosperity and dynastic continuity.
76: **Tuus** (possessive adj., nom. sg. masc.) "yours/your," **O regina** (voc. sg. fem.) "O queen," **quid** (interrog. pron., acc. sg. neut.) "what," **optes** (pres. subjunct., 2nd sg.) "you wish/desire," **Aeolus** (nom. sg. masc.) "Aeolus," **contra** (adv.) "in reply." Aeolus responds to Juno, emphasizing that his duty is to discern and fulfill whatever she, the queen, desires.
77: **explorare** (pres. act. inf., "to investigate/ascertain") **labor** (nom. sg., "task/duty"), **mihi** (dat. sg., "for me") **iussa** (acc. pl. neut., "commands") **capessere** (pres. act. inf., "to undertake/execute"), **fas** (indecl. nom./acc., "divine law/right"). Aeolus responds to Juno: "Yours is the task to investigate what you wish; for me it is right to undertake your commands," establishing the hierarchical relationship where he merely obeys her divine will.
78: **Tu** (pronoun, nominative, "you") **mihi** (pronoun, dative, "to/for me") **quodcumque hoc regni** (pronoun + pronoun + genitive, "whatever of kingdom/this of kingdom") **tu sceptra** (pronoun nominative + accusative plural, "you, the scepters") **Iovemque** (accusative + enclitic, "and Jupiter"). Dido addresses her sister Anna, crediting her with granting whatever royal power she possesses, the symbols of authority (sceptra), and favorable relations with Jupiter; the repetition of *tu* emphasizes Anna's agency as benefactor.
79: **concilias** (2nd sg. pres. act. indic. of *conciliō, -āre*) "you bring into harmony, reconcile"; **das** (2nd sg. pres. act. indic. of *dō, dare*) "you grant, give"; **epulis** (dat./abl. pl. of *epulae, -ārum* f.) "at the feasts"; **accumbere** (pres. act. inf. of *accumbō, -ere*) "to recline"; **divom** (gen. pl. of *deus, -ī* m., archaic form = *divōrum*) "of the gods." Juno continues addressing Aeolus: you reconcile favor, you grant him to recline at the gods' banquets (subject of both verbs remains Jupiter from the previous line).
80:
**nimborumque facis tempestatumque potentem.**

*nimborum* (genitive plural of *nimbus*, "of storms/rainclouds") and *tempestatumque* (genitive plural of *tempestas*, "of tempests/weather") depend on *potentem* (accusative singular adjective, "powerful over/master of"). *facis* (2nd person singular present active indicative of *facio*, "you make") governs *potentem* as object complement, referring to the god being addressed (likely Neptune or another deity). Juno continues her flattery: "you make [him] master of storms and tempests."
81:
**Haec ubi dicta, cavum conversa cuspide montem**

*Haec* (neut. pl. acc., demonstrative pronoun) "these things"; *dicta* (perf. pass. participle from *dico*, neut. pl. nom./acc.) "having been said"; *cavum* (adj., masc. acc. sg.) "hollow"; *conversa* (perf. pass. participle from *converto*, nom./abl. fem. sg.) "having turned"; *cuspide* (fem. abl. sg., *cuspis*) "with his spear-point"; *montem* (masc. acc. sg., *mons*) "mountain." When these things had been said, Aeolus struck the hollow mountain with his turned spear-point (the ablative absolute *conversa cuspide* indicates the instrument).
82:
**impulit in latus: ac venti, velut agmine facto,**

*impulit* (3rd sg. perf. act. indic. of *impello*) "drove/thrust"; *latus* (acc. neut. sg.) "side/flank"; *venti* (nom. masc. pl.) "winds"; *velut* (adv.) "just as/like"; *agmine* (abl. neut. sg. of *agmen*) "battle-line/column," with *facto* (abl. neut. sg. perf. pass. part. of *facio*) "having been formed." Aeolus thrust his spear into the mountain's side, and the winds, as if a battle formation had been formed, rush forth in military array.
83:
**qua data porta, ruunt et terras turbine perflant.**

*qua* (relative adverb, "where/by which way"), *data* (perfect passive participle from *do*, ablative feminine singular modifying *porta*, "having been given/granted"), *porta* (ablative singular, "gate/opening"), *ruunt* (3rd plural present indicative of *ruo*, "they rush"), *turbine* (ablative singular of *turbo*, "with a whirlwind/storm"), *perflant* (3rd plural present of *perflo*, "they blow through"). The winds rush through the granted opening and blast through the lands with whirlwind force.
84:
**Incubuere mari, totumque a sedibus imis**

*Incubuere* (perf. indic. 3rd pl. of *incumbo*) "they press upon/fall upon"; *mari* (dat. sg.) "upon the sea"; *totum* (acc. sg. neut.) "the whole [sea]"; *sedibus* (abl. pl.) "from its seats/foundations"; *imis* (abl. pl. superl. adj.) "deepest/lowest." The winds violently bear down upon the sea and churn it up entirely from its deepest foundations.
85: **una** (adv.) = together, at once; **Eurus** (nom. m. sg.) = the East wind; **Notus** (nom. m. sg.) = the South wind; **ruunt** (3rd pl. pres. ind. act., *ruo*) = rush, storm forth; **creber** (nom. m. sg.) = thick, frequent; **procellis** (abl. f. pl.) = with storms, squalls. The East and South winds rush forth together, and [another wind] thick with storms—a hendiadys of violent convergence as multiple winds assault the sea simultaneously.
86: **Africus** (nom. sg., subject) "the southwest wind," **vastos** (acc. pl. masc., modifying *fluctus*) "vast, huge," **volvunt** (3rd pl. pres. act. ind.) "roll, drive," **litora** (acc. pl. neut.) "shores," **fluctus** (acc. pl. masc., direct object) "waves." The southwest wind joins the East and South winds in rolling massive waves toward the shore, completing the catalog of storm winds unleashed by Aeolus.
87: **Insequitur** (verb, 3rd sg. pres. ind., "follows upon" or "ensues") **clamorque** (noun, nom. sg. with -que, "and the shouting") **virum** (noun, gen. pl., "of men") **stridorque** (noun, nom. sg. with -que, "and the screeching/whistling") **rudentum** (noun, gen. pl., "of the ropes/rigging"). The storm's violence is immediately followed by the clamor of sailors and the shrieking of the ship's rigging under strain.
88: **Eripiunt** (3rd pl. pres. act. ind., *eripio*) "snatch away"; **subito** (adv.) "suddenly"; **nubes** (nom. pl., *nubes*) "clouds" (subject); **caelumque diemque** (acc. pl., *caelum* and *dies*, connected by *-que*...*-que*) "both sky and daylight" (objects of *eripiunt*). The clouds suddenly snatch away both sky and daylight from the Trojans' eyes, as the storm erupts.
89: **Teucrorum** (gen. pl., "of the Trojans/Teucrians") **ex oculis** (abl. pl., "from the eyes") **ponto** (dat./abl. sg., "on the sea") **nox** (nom. sg., "night") **incubat** (3rd sg. pres., "lies upon/broods over") **atra** (nom. sg. fem., "black/dark"). The clouds snatch sky and daylight from the Trojans' sight; black night settles upon the sea.
90: **Intonuere** (perf. ind. act., 3rd pl. of *intono*) "thundered" – the heavens resounded. **poli** (nom. pl., *polus*) "the heavens/skies" – subject of the verb. **crebris ignibus** (abl. pl., *creber* + *ignis*) "with frequent fires/flashes" – describes the lightning. **micat** (pres. ind. act., 3rd sg. of *mico*) "flashes/gleams" – **aether** (nom. sg., *aether*) "the upper air/sky" – flashes with repeated lightning bolts. The heavens thunder and the sky flashes with constant lightning, intensifying the storm's fury.
91:
**praesentemque viris intentant omnia mortem.**

*praesentem* (adj., acc. sg. f.) modifying *mortem*, "immediate" or "present"; *viris* (noun, dat. pl. m.) "for the men"; *intentant* (verb, 3rd pl. pres. act. indic.) "threaten" or "portend"; *omnia* (adj./pron., nom. pl. n.) "all things" serving as subject; *mortem* (noun, acc. sg. f.) "death." All things threaten immediate death to the men, as the storm's fury portends their imminent destruction.
92:
**Extemplo Aeneae solvuntur frigore membra:**

*Extemplo* (adv., "immediately"), *Aeneae* (gen. sg., "of Aeneas"), *solvuntur* (pres. pass. indic. 3rd pl., "are loosened/grow weak"), *frigore* (abl. sg., "with/by cold/chill"), *membra* (nom. pl. neut., "limbs"). Immediately Aeneas' limbs grow weak with cold—a vivid description of the physical effects of sudden terror as he faces the storm at sea.
93:
**ingemit, et duplicis tendens ad sidera palmas**

*ingemit* (3rd sg. pres. ind. of *ingemo*) "he groans"; *duplicis* (acc. pl. f. of *duplex*) "double, both"; *tendens* (pres. part. of *tendo*) "stretching, extending"; *sidera* (acc. pl. n. of *sidus*) "stars, heavens"; *palmas* (acc. pl. f. of *palma*) "palms, hands." Aeneas groans and stretches both hands toward the stars in a gesture of supplication or despair.
94:
**Target:** *O terque quaterque beati, talia voce refert:*

**terque quaterque** (adverbs) "three and four times" = seven times, emphatically "many times over"; **beati** (nominative plural adjective/substantive) "blessed ones, fortunate ones"; **talia** (neuter plural accusative, demonstrative pronoun) "such things"; **voce** (ablative singular of *vox*) "with his voice"; **refert** (3rd singular present indicative of *referre*) "he speaks, utters." Aeneas addresses those who died at Troy as supremely fortunate, introducing his lament with ritualized emphasis.
95:
**Gloss for "quis ante ora patrum Troiae sub moenibus altis":**

*quis* (relative/interrogative pronoun, dative plural) "for whom"; *ante* (preposition + accusative) "before"; *ora* (noun, accusative plural, n. of *os*) "faces, presence"; *patrum* (noun, genitive plural of *pater*) "of fathers, ancestors"; *moenibus altis* (noun + adjective, ablative plural) "beneath the lofty walls." Aeneas continues his apostrophe, identifying those blessed who died before their fathers' eyes beneath Troy's towering fortifications.
96:
**contigit oppetere! O Danaum fortissime gentis**

*contigit* (3rd sing. perf. ind. of *contingō*) = "it befell, was granted"; *oppetere* (pres. act. inf. of *oppetō*) = "to meet death, perish"; *Danaum* (gen. pl. of *Danaī*) = "of the Greeks"; *fortissime* (voc. sing. masc. superl. of *fortis*) = "O bravest"; *gentis* (gen. sing. of *gēns*) = "of the race, people." 

Aeneas laments that Diomedes, the bravest of the Greeks, was granted the privilege of dying gloriously at Troy, unlike his own inglorious fate of shipwreck.
97: **Tydide!** (vocative singular of *Tydides*) "son of Tydeus" = Diomedes; **Mene** (accusative singular of *ego* + enclitic *-ne*) "me" (interrogative); **Iliacis** (ablative plural of *Iliacus, -a, -um*) "Trojan"; **occumbere** (present infinitive of *occumbo*) "to fall in death, to die"; **campis** (ablative plural of *campus*) "on the plains." Aeneas laments that he could not die by Diomedes' hand on the Trojan plains, an honorable death befitting a warrior.
98: **non potuisse** (perfect active infinitive of *possum*): "to have been unable," expressing the regret that she could not die at Troy. **tuaque ... dextra** (ablative of means with *tua*, "your"): "by your right hand," referring to Diomedes' weapon. **animam** (accusative singular of *anima*): "life" or "soul," the object of *effundere*. **effundere** (perfect active infinitive of *effundo*): "to pour out," i.e., to give up in death. Dido laments that she was not permitted to fall on the Trojan plains and surrender her life to Diomedes' spear.
99: **saevus** (adj., nom. sg. m.) "fierce/savage"; **Aeacidae** (noun, gen. sg. m.) "of the descendant of Aeacus" (i.e., Achilles); **telo** (noun, abl. sg. n.) "by the weapon/spear"; **iacet** (verb, 3rd sg. pres. ind.) "lies (dead)"; **Hector** (proper noun, nom. sg. m.) "Hector." The speaker laments where fierce Hector lies slain by the weapon of Achilles, continuing a catalog of places associated with Trojan deaths, introduced by the repeated "ubi."
100: **Sarpedon** (nom. sg., proper name) – Sarpedon, the Lycian hero and son of Zeus slain by Patroclus; **tot** (indecl. adj.) – so many; **Simois** (nom. sg., proper name) – the Simoïs, river at Troy; **correpta** (perf. pass. part., nom./acc. pl. n.) – seized, snatched away; **sub undis** (abl. pl. with prep.) – beneath the waves. The line continues the catalog of Trojan casualties, asking where Sarpedon lies and noting how many shields and helmets the Simoïs river has swept beneath its waters.
101: **scuta** (n. acc. pl., < *scutum*) "shields"; **virum** (gen. pl., < *vir*) "of men"; **galeasque** (acc. pl., < *galea*) "and helmets"; **fortia corpora** (acc. pl., neut. adj. + n., < *fortis* + *corpus*) "strong/brave bodies"; **volvit** (3rd sg. pres., < *volvo*) "rolls/tosses." The Simois river rolls along shields, helmets, and the brave bodies of warriors swept beneath its waves.
102:
**Talia iactanti stridens Aquilone procella**

*Talia* (neut. acc. pl., "such things") is the object of *iactanti* (pres. act. part., dat./abl. sg. from *iacio*, "hurling/shouting"), referring to Aeneas speaking. *Stridens* (pres. act. part., nom. sg. from *strido*, "shrieking/whistling") modifies *procella* (nom. sg., "storm"), the subject. *Aquilone* (abl. sg., "from the North Wind" or "with the North Wind") indicates origin or accompaniment. The storm shrieks from the north upon Aeneas as he utters such words.
103: **velum** (n., acc. sg.) "sail" – object of *ferit*; **adversa** (adj., nom. sg. fem.) "head-on" or "opposing" – modifying *procella* from the previous line; **ferit** (v., 3rd sg. pres.) "strikes"; **fluctusque** (n., acc. pl.) "and the waves" – object of *tollit*; **sidera** (n., acc. pl.) "stars" – limit of motion with *ad*; **tollit** (v., 3rd sg. pres.) "lifts/raises." The storm strikes the sail head-on and lifts the waves up to the stars, depicting the tempest's violent force.
104: **Franguntur** (*frangō*, 3rd pl. pres. pass. ind.) "are shattered/broken" — the oars snap under strain. **remi** (nom. pl. m.) "oars." **prora** (nom. sg. f.) "prow/bow" — the front of the ship. **avertit** (*āvertō*, 3rd sg. pres. act. ind.) "turns away" — the bow swings around. **undis** (dat./abl. pl. f.) "to/for the waves" — presenting the ship's vulnerable side to the sea's assault.
105:
**dat latus; insequitur cumulo praeruptus aquae mons.**

*dat* (3rd sg. pres. act. ind. of *do*) "gives, exposes"; *latus* (n. acc. sg.) "side, flank"; *insequitur* (3rd sg. pres. dep. ind. of *insequor*) "follows, pursues"; *praeruptus* (nom. sg. m. perf. pass. part.) "steep, headlong"; *mons* (nom. sg. m.) "mountain, mass." The ship exposes its vulnerable side to the waves, and a towering, sheer mountain of water follows in a heap upon it.
106:
**Hi summo in fluctu pendent; his unda dehiscens**

*Hi* (nom. pl. m., "these men/ships") and *his* (dat. pl. m., "for these") establish antithesis between two groups of sailors. *Summo in fluctu* (abl. sg. m., "on the highest wave") locates the first group at the crest. *Pendent* (3rd pl. pres. act. indic. of *pendeo*, "hang, are suspended") describes their precarious position. *Unda dehiscens* (nom. sg. f., "the gaping wave" – pres. act. participle of *dehisco*, "gape open, split apart") introduces the opposite peril facing the second group in the wave's trough.
107: **terram** (acc. sing. f., "land/ground"), **inter** (prep. + acc., "between/amid"), **fluctus** (acc. pl. m., "waves"), **aperit** (pres. 3rd sing., "opens/reveals"), **furit** (pres. 3rd sing., "rages"), **aestus** (nom. sing. m., "surge/boiling"), **harenis** (abl. pl. f., "with sands/in the sands"). The wave opens up the land between the waters, and the surge boils furiously with sand churned up from the seabed.
108:
**Tris Notus abreptas in saxa latentia torquet—**

*Tris* (acc. pl. adj., "three"), *Notus* (nom. sg., "the South Wind," subject), *abreptas* (acc. pl. f. perf. pass. part. from *abripio*, modifying ships understood, "snatched away"), *latentia* (acc. pl. n. pres. act. part. from *lateo*, modifying *saxa*, "hidden/lurking"), *torquet* (3rd sg. pres. act. indic., "twists/hurls"). The South Wind hurls three ships, snatched away by the storm, onto hidden rocks.
109:
**saxa vocant Itali mediis quae in fluctibus aras—**

*saxa* (n. acc. pl., "rocks"); *vocant* (3rd pl. pres. act., "call"); *Itali* (m. nom. pl., "the Italians"); *mediis...in fluctibus* (abl. pl., "in the midst of the waves"); *aras* (f. acc. pl., "altars"). The Italians call these rocks "the Altars," which lie in the middle of the waves—a notorious reef formation.
110:
**dorsum immane mari summo; tris Eurus ab alto**

*dorsum* (n. acc. sg.) "back, reef" – the submerged rocky ridge; *immane* (adj. acc. sg. n.) "monstrous, huge" modifying *dorsum*; *mari summo* (abl. sg.) "on the surface of the sea"; *tris* = *teris* (2nd sg. pres. indic.) "you grind, wear away"; *Eurus* (nom. sg.) "the East wind" as subject; *ab alto* (abl. sg.) "from the deep." The East wind grinds ships upon the monstrous reef lying just beneath the sea's surface.
111:
**Target: in brevia et Syrtis urguet, miserabile visu,**

*brevia* (n. acc. pl., "shallows, shoals"), *Syrtis* (f. acc. pl., "the Syrtes," sandbanks off North Africa), *urguet* (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of *urgeo*, "drives, forces"), *miserabile* (n. acc. sg. adj., "pitiable, wretched"), *visu* (m. abl. sg. supine of *video*, "to see," in ablative of respect). Eurus drives [the ships] into the shallows and Syrtes—a sight pitiable to behold.
112:
**inliditque vadis atque aggere cingit harenae.**

*inlidit* (3rd sg. pres. indic. act. of *illido*) "dashes upon"; *vadis* (abl. pl. of *vadum*) "shallows, shoals"; *aggere* (abl. sg. of *agger*) "mound, heap"; *cingit* (3rd sg. pres. indic. act. of *cingo*) "surrounds, encircles"; *harenae* (gen. sg. of *harena*) "of sand." The ship is dashed upon the shallows and surrounded by a mound of sand, describing its grounding and entrapment.
113:
**Unam, quae Lycios fidumque vehebat Oronten,**

*Unam* (acc. fem. sing. of *unus*, "one [ship]") is the direct object. *quae* (nom. fem. sing. relative pronoun, "which") introduces a relative clause. *Lycios* (acc. masc. pl. of *Lycius*, "Lycians") and *Oronten* (acc. masc. sing., "Orontes") are both objects of *vehebat* (imperf. act. indic. 3rd sing. of *veho*, "was carrying"). *fidum* (acc. masc. sing. of *fidus*, "faithful/loyal") modifies *Oronten*.
114:
**ipsius ante oculos ingens a vertice pontus**

*ipsius* (gen. sing. of *ipse*) "of him himself" (i.e., Aeneas); *ante oculos* (prep. + acc. pl.) "before the eyes"; *ingens* (nom. sing. adj.) "huge, massive"; *a vertice* (prep. + abl. sing.) "from the crest/top"; *pontus* (nom. sing.) "sea, wave." Before Aeneas's very eyes, a massive wave strikes from its crest, introducing the catastrophic blow that follows in the next line.
115:
**in puppim ferit: excutitur pronusque magister**

*puppim* (acc. sg. of *puppis*, f.) = "stern" (of the ship); *ferit* (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of *ferio*) = "strikes"; *excutitur* (3rd sg. pres. pass. indic. of *excutio*) = "is hurled out/shaken off"; *pronusque* = "and headlong" (*pronus*, nom. sg. m., modifying *magister*); *magister* (nom. sg. m.) = "helmsman." The wave strikes the stern, and the helmsman is violently thrown out headlong.
116:
**volvitur in caput; ast illam ter fluctus ibidem**

*volvitur* (3rd sg. pres. pass. ind. of *volvo*) "is rolled/tumbled," the helmsman spins headlong; *caput* (acc. sg. n.) "head," indicating the direction of his fall; *ast* (conj.) "but," marking the shift to the ship's fate; *fluctus* (nom. sg. m.) "wave/billow," subject of the following action; *ter* (adv.) "three times," emphasizing the repetition of the wave's battering; *ibidem* (adv.) "in the same place," the ship trapped in one spot.
117: **torquet** (verb, 3rd sg. pres. ind.) "twists/whirls"; **agens** (verb, pres. part. nom. sg.) "driving"; **circum** (adv.) "around/in a circle"; **rapidus** (adj. nom. sg. m.) "swift/raging"; **vorat** (verb, 3rd sg. pres. ind.) "devours/swallows up"; **vortex** (noun, nom. sg. m.) "whirlpool/vortex". The swift whirlpool twists and drives the ship around in circles, then devours it in the sea.
118: **Adparent** (3rd pl. pres. ind. of *adpareo*) "appear," **rari** (nom. pl. masc. adj.) "scattered/few," **nantes** (nom. pl. masc. pres. part. of *no*) "swimming," **gurgite** (abl. sg. of *gurges*) "in the whirlpool/abyss," **vasto** (abl. sg. masc. adj.) "vast/enormous." A few scattered swimmers appear in the vast whirlpool, describing survivors struggling in the sea after the shipwreck.
119: **arma** (n. nom./acc. pl., "arms, equipment"), **virum** (gen. pl., "of men"), **tabulae** (nom. pl., "planks, timbers"), **gaza** (nom. sg., "treasure, wealth"), **undas** (acc. pl., "waves"). The scattered debris of the Trojan fleet becomes visible: weapons, men's gear, ship planks, and Trojan treasure are seen floating through the waves after the storm's destruction.
120:
**Iam validam Ilionei navem, iam fortis Achati,**

*validam* (adj., acc. sg. fem.) "strong"; *Ilionei* (proper noun, gen. sg.) "of Ilioneus"; *navem* (noun, acc. sg. fem.) "ship"; *fortis* (adj., gen. sg. masc.) "brave/strong"; *Achati* (proper noun, gen. sg.) "of Achates." The storm now assails the sturdy ship of Ilioneus and that of brave Achates, with possessive genitives marking the vessels' ownership by these Trojan companions.
121:
**et qua vectus Abas, et qua grandaevus Aletes,**

*vectus* (perf. pass. part. of *veho*, nom. sg. masc.) "having been carried"; *Abas* (nom. sg.) the Trojan hero Abas; *qua* (abl. sg. fem. of *qui*) "in/on which" (sc. *nave*); *grandaevus* (adj., nom. sg. masc.) "aged, venerable"; *Aletes* (nom. sg.) the elderly Trojan Aletes. The anaphoric *et qua...et qua* construction parallels the ships carrying Abas and old Aletes, both now overcome by the storm.
122:
**vicit hiems; laxis laterum compagibus omnes**

*vicit* (perf. act. ind. 3rd sg. of *vinco*) "conquered, prevailed"; *hiems* (nom. sg. f.) "the storm, winter weather"; *laxis* (abl. pl. f. of *laxus*) "loosened, slack"; *laterum* (gen. pl. n. of *latus*) "of the sides"; *compagibus* (abl. pl. f. of *compages*) "joints, fastenings." The storm has conquered; all the ships' side-fastenings having been loosened, they receive the hostile rain and split apart at the seams.
123:
**accipiunt inimicum imbrem, rimisque fatiscunt.**

Key words: *accipiunt* (3rd pl. pres. act. ind., "they receive"), *inimicum* (acc. sg. masc. adj., "hostile/harmful"), *imbrem* (acc. sg. masc., "rain/water"), *rimis* (abl. pl. fem., "through cracks"), *fatiscunt* (3rd pl. pres. act. ind., "they gape open/fall apart"). The ships take on destructive seawater through their loosened seams and split apart at the cracks.
124: **Interea** (adv., "meanwhile") **magno** (adj., abl. sing. masc./neut., "great/loud," modifying *murmure*) **misceri** (pres. pass. inf., "to be stirred up/thrown into confusion") **murmure** (noun, abl. sing., "roar/rumbling," ablative of manner) **pontum** (noun, acc. sing., "sea/deep," subject of the infinitive). Meanwhile the sea is stirred up with a great roar; this indirect statement introduces Neptune's awareness of the storm Aeolus has unleashed at Juno's command.
125:
**emissamque hiemem sensit Neptunus, et imis**

*emissam* (perf. pass. partic., acc. fem. sing. from *emitto*) "sent forth, unleashed"; *hiemem* (acc. fem. sing.) "storm, winter tempest"; *sensit* (perf. 3rd sing. from *sentio*) "perceived, felt"; *Neptunus* (nom. masc. sing.) "Neptune" (god of the sea); *imis* (abl. neut. plur. from *imus*) "from the depths." Neptune perceived that the storm had been unleashed, introducing the sea-god's awareness of Aeolus's interference with his domain.
126:
**stagna refusa vadis, graviter commotus; et alto**

*stagna* (n. acc. pl., "pools, waters") *refusa* (perf. pass. part., "poured back, flooded") *vadis* (abl. pl., "onto the shallows") — Neptune observes the waters flooded back onto the shallows. *graviter* (adv., "deeply, heavily") *commotus* (perf. pass. part., "moved, disturbed") — he is deeply disturbed by the disruption. *alto* (abl. n. sg., "from the deep") connects to the next line, positioning Neptune rising from the depths.
127: **prospiciens** (pres. part., nom. sg. m.) "looking out/surveying"; **summa** (abl. sg. f.) "from the top of"; **placidum** (acc. sg. n.) "calm, peaceful"; **caput** (acc. sg. n.) "head"; **extulit** (perf., 3rd sg.) "raised, lifted up"; **unda** (abl. sg. f.) "wave, water." Neptune, looking out over the sea, raised his calm head from the surface of the water, surveying Aeneas's scattered fleet across the expanse.
128: **Disiectam** (perfect passive participle, accusative feminine singular, from *disicio*) "scattered" modifies *classem*. **Aeneae** (genitive singular) "of Aeneas" depends on *classem*. **toto ... aequore** (ablative of place where) "over the whole sea." **videt** (third-person singular present active indicative) "sees." **classem** (accusative singular) "fleet," direct object of *videt*. Neptune sees Aeneas's fleet scattered over the whole sea.
129:
**fluctibus oppressos Troas caelique ruina,**

*fluctibus* (m. abl. pl. of *fluctus*) "by the waves"; *oppressos* (perf. pass. part. acc. m. pl. of *opprimo*) "overwhelmed, crushed"; *Troas* (acc. m. pl. of *Troas*) "the Trojans"; *caeli* (gen. sg. of *caelum*) "of the sky"; *ruina* (abl. sg. of *ruina*) "by the ruin, collapse." The Trojans are overwhelmed by the waves and by the collapse/destruction from the sky (Jupiter's storm).
130:
**nec latuere doli fratrem Iunonis et irae.**

*latuere* (perfect, "escaped the notice of") governs *fratrem* (accusative, "brother," i.e., Neptune); *doli* and *irae* (nominative plural subjects, "the tricks and anger") refer to Juno's scheming; *fratrem Iunonis* identifies Neptune as Juno's brother. The line means "nor did the tricks and anger of Juno escape her brother's notice."
131: **Eurum** (acc. sg., Greek name) "the East Wind," **Zephyrumque** (acc. sg., Greek name) "and the West Wind" – direct objects of **vocat** (3rd sg. pres. act. indic., "he/she calls"). **Dehinc** (adv.) "thereupon, next," **talia** (acc. pl. neut., "such things") – object of **fatur** (3rd sg. pres. dep. indic., "he/she speaks"). Aeolus summons two principal winds and begins his address to them.
132: **Tantane** (interrog. adv.) "so great" modifies *fiducia*; **generis** (gen. sing., neut.) "of birth/lineage"; **tenuit** (perf. act. indic., 3rd sing., *teneo*) "held/seized"; **fiducia** (nom. sing., fem.) "confidence/presumption"; **vestri** (gen. sing., masc.) "of your own" modifying *generis*. Juno rebukes the winds: "Has so great a confidence in your own birth/station seized you?"
133: **caelum** (noun, acc. sg.) "sky, heaven"; **terramque** (noun, acc. sg. with enclitic -que) "and earth"; **numine** (noun, abl. sg.) "divine will, power"; **sine** (preposition + abl.) "without"; **venti** (noun, voc. pl.) "O winds." Neptune rebukes the winds for daring to confound sky and earth without his divine authority, establishing the hierarchical order among the gods.
134:
**miscere** (pres. inf., "to mix/stir up"), **et** (conj., "and"), **tantas** (acc. pl. f., "such great"), **audetis** (2nd pl. pres. ind., "you dare"), **tollere** (pres. inf., "to raise/lift up"), **moles** (acc. pl. f., "masses/structures"). 

Neptune rebukes the winds for daring to churn up the sea and sky and raise such enormous waves without his divine authorization, an angry interrogative expressing his outrage at their presumption.
135:
**Quos ego—sed motos praestat componere fluctus.**

*Quos* (relative pronoun, acc. pl. masc.) = "whom" (object of implied verb of punishment). *Ego* (personal pronoun, nom. sing.) = "I" (Neptune breaking off his threat). *Motos* (perfect passive participle, acc. pl. masc., from *moveo*) = "disturbed/stirred up." *Praestat* (verb, 3rd sing. pres. act. indic., from *praesto*) = "it is better/preferable." *Componere* (infinitive, pres. act.) = "to calm/settle." Neptune interrupts his threat (*aposiopesis*) to prioritize calming the storm-tossed waves over punishing the winds.
136: **Post** (adv., "hereafter, in the future") **mihi** (dat. of ego, "to me, before me") **non** (neg. particle) **simili** (abl. of similis, modifying poena, "with a similar") **poena** (abl. of poena, "penalty, punishment") **commissa** (neut. pl. acc. of commissum, "offenses, crimes") **luetis** (2nd pl. fut. of luo, "you will pay for, atone for"). Neptune warns the winds that future transgressions will not be punished with mere verbal rebuke but with far severer consequences.
137:
**Maturate fugam, regique haec dicite vestro:**

*Maturate* (2nd pl. pres. imper. act. of *maturo*) = "hasten"; *fugam* (acc. sg. f.) = "flight, escape"; *regi* (dat. sg. m.) = "to the king"; *haec* (acc. pl. n.) = "these things"; *dicite* (2nd pl. pres. imper. act. of *dico*) = "say, tell"; *vestro* (dat. sg. m.) = "your." Neptune commands the winds to hasten their flight and report his words to their king Aeolus, asserting his own supreme authority over the sea.
138:
**non illi imperium pelagi saevumque tridentem,**

*imperium* (n. nom./acc. sg.) "power, sovereignty"; *pelagi* (n. gen. sg. from *pelagus*) "of the sea"; *saevum* (adj. acc. sg. n.) "savage, cruel"; *tridentem* (m. acc. sg.) "trident." Neptune asserts that Neptune (the speaker), not Jupiter (*illi* dative of possession), holds dominion over the sea and its fearsome trident—establishing territorial divine authority.
139: **sorte** (ablative singular of *sors*) "by lot, by allotment"; **datum** (perfect passive participle of *do*, accusative neuter singular agreeing with *imperium*) "given"; **tenet** (3rd singular present active of *teneo*) "he holds, possesses"; **immania** (accusative neuter plural of *immanis*) "monstrous, huge"; **saxa** (accusative neuter plural of *saxum*) "rocks, crags." Neptune contrasts his divinely allotted sea-dominion with Aeolus's assigned realm of massive rocky caves.
140:
**vestras, Eure, domos; illa se iactet in aula**

*vestras* (adj., acc. pl. fem.) "your" modifies *domos*; *Eure* (voc. sg. m.) "Eurus" (the East Wind), vocative address; *domos* (acc. pl. fem.) "homes, halls"; *illa* (abl. sg. fem.) "in that" refers to the domain just mentioned; *iactet* (pres. subj. 3rd sg.) "let him boast, swagger." Juno tells Aeolus to confine himself to the winds' realm, letting Aeolus strut about in that hall rather than anywhere else.
141: **Aeolus** (nom. sg., proper noun) "Aeolus"; **clauso** (abl. sg. m., perfect passive participle of *claudo*) "closed, shut up"; **ventorum** (gen. pl. m., *ventus*) "of the winds"; **carcere** (abl. sg. m., *carcer*) "in the prison"; **regnet** (3rd sg. pres. subj., *regno*) "let him rule/reign." Venus tells Aeolus to rule from his palace while keeping the winds shut in their prison.
142:
**Gloss:**

*Sic* (adv., "thus") introduces Neptune's swift action. *ait* (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of *aio*, "he speaks"). *dicto* (abl. sg. neut. of *dictum*, "than the word/speech," with comparative *citius*). *citius* (comp. adv., "more swiftly"). *tumida* (nom./acc. pl. neut. of *tumidus*, "swollen") modifies *aequora*. *aequora* (acc. pl. neut. of *aequor*, "seas/waters," dir. obj. of *placat*). *placat* (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of *placo*, "he calms").
143:
**collectasque fugat nubes, solemque reducit.**

*collectas* (perf. pass. part. acc. fem. pl. from *colligo*) "gathered," modifying *nubes*; *fugat* (pres. act. ind. 3rd sg. from *fugo*) "puts to flight, disperses"; *nubes* (acc. fem. pl.) "clouds"; *solemque* (*solem* + *-que*) "and the sun" (acc. masc. sg.); *reducit* (pres. act. ind. 3rd sg. from *reduco*) "leads back, restores." Neptune disperses the storm clouds he has gathered and brings back the sunlight.
144:
**Cymothoe simul et Triton adnixus acuto**

*Cymothoe* (nom. sg., Greek name): sea-nymph Cymothoe, subject with Triton; *simul* (adv.): at the same time, together; *Triton* (nom. sg.): sea-god Triton, joint subject; *adnixus* (perf. part. nom. sg. m.): having pressed against, straining with; *acuto* (abl. sg. n.): with his sharp (trident, understood from context). The sea-nymph Cymothoe and the god Triton work together, Triton straining with his sharp trident to free Neptune's ships from the rocks.
145:
**detrudunt navis scopulo; levat ipse tridenti;**

*detrudunt* (3rd pl. pres. act. ind. of *detrudo*) "they thrust down/dislodge"; *navis* (acc. pl. f.) "the ships"; *scopulo* (abl. sing. m.) "from the rock/reef"; *levat* (3rd sing. pres. act. ind. of *levo*) "he lifts/raises"; *tridenti* (abl. sing. m.) "with his trident." Neptune personally assists Cymothoe and Triton by lifting ships with his trident, dislodging them from the rocks where they are grounded.
146:
**et vastas aperit syrtis, et temperat aequor,**

*aperit* (3rd sg. pres. ind. act., *aperio*) "opens up"; *syrtis* (acc. pl., *syrtis* f.) "sandbanks, shoals"; *vastas* (acc. pl. f., *vastus*) "vast, extensive"; *temperat* (3rd sg. pres. ind. act., *tempero*) "calms, controls"; *aequor* (acc. sg. n., *aequor*) "sea, level surface." Neptune opens up the vast sandbanks (making passage possible) and calms the sea with his trident.
147:
**atque** (conj.) "and"; **rotis** (abl. pl. of *rota*, f.) "with wheels/chariots"; **summas** (acc. pl. f. of *summus*) "topmost, surface"; **levibus** (abl. pl. of *levis*) "light, swift"; **perlabitur** (3rd sg. pres. ind. of *perlabor*, deponent) "glides over." 

Neptune glides over the topmost waves with his swift chariot wheels, calming the storm-tossed sea after opening the sandbanks and tempering the waters.
148:
**Ac veluti magno in populo cum saepe coorta est**

*veluti* (adv.) "just as"; *magno in populo* (abl. of place) "in a great populace/nation"; *cum* (conj.) "when"; *saepe* (adv.) "often"; *coorta est* (perf. indic., 3rd sg. of *coorior*) "has arisen." This simile introduces a comparison between Neptune calming the waves and a statesman quelling civil unrest, with *seditio* as the understood subject carried over from the next line.
149:
**seditio, saevitque animis ignobile volgus,**

*seditio* (nom. sg. f.): "sedition, civil strife" (subject of understood verb); *saevit* (pres. ind. 3rd sg.): "rages, acts savagely" (*-que* = "and"); *animis* (abl. pl. m.): "in their spirits/passions" (ablative of respect or means); *ignobile* (nom. sg. n.): "lowborn, base"; *volgus* (nom. sg. n.): "the mob, common crowd" (subject). The sedition erupts and the base mob rages in its passions, continuing the extended simile of civil unrest.
150:
**iamque faces et saxa volant—furor arma ministrat;**

"then"; **pietate** (abl. of *pietas*) "in devotion/duty"; **gravem** (acc. masc. sing. of *gravis*) "weighty, respected," modifying *virum*; **meritis** (abl. pl. of *meritum*) "in achievements/services"; **virum** (acc. masc. sing. of *vir*) "man." "father" [Neptune] — **caeloque** (dat. sing., -que "and") "and to/in the sky" — **invectus** (perf. part., nom. sing. masc.) "having been borne, riding" — **aperto** (abl. sing. neut.) "open, clear." The father Neptune, looking out over the sea, rides through the now-clear sky, having calmed the storm.

The weary Trojans strain to reach the nearest coastline and turn toward the shores of Libya.

**Est in secessu longo locus: insula portum**

*est* (3rd sg. pres. ind. of *sum*) "there is"; *secessu* (abl. sg. m. of *secessus*) "in a recess/withdrawal"; *longo* (abl. sg. m. of *longus*) "deep/far-extending"; *locus* (nom. sg. m.) "a place"; *insula* (nom. sg. f.) "an island"; *portum* (acc. sg. m. of *portus*) "harbor" (object of *efficit* in the following line). This introduces the harbor at Libya where Aeneas's fleet will find refuge; the island forms a harbor through the projection of its sides.

**efficit obiectu laterum, quibus omnis ab alto**

*efficit* (3rd sg. pres. act. ind. of *efficiō*) "makes" or "forms" — the island creates the harbor; *obiectū* (abl. sg. masc. of *obiectus*, -ūs) "by the blocking" or "by the projection" — ablative of means; *laterum* (gen. pl. neut. of *latus*, lateris) "of the sides" — the island's flanking promontories; *quibus* (abl. pl. neut. of *quī*, relative pronoun) "by which" or "off which"; *ab altō* (abl. sg. neut. of *altum*) "from the deep sea." 161:
**frangitur** (3rd sg. pres. pass. indic. of *frango*) "is broken"; **sinus** (acc. pl. m. of *sinus*) "bays, curves"; **scindit** (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of *scindo*) "splits, divides"; **sese** (acc. of reflexive *se*) "itself"; **reductos** (acc. pl. m. perf. pass. part. of *reduco*) "drawn back, receding."

The wave breaks upon the barrier of rocks and divides itself into the receding bays formed by the lateral projections, describing how the harbor's architecture channels incoming water into protected inlets.
162:
**Hinc atque hinc vastae rupes geminique minantur**

*hinc atque hinc* (adv.) "on this side and on that," "on both sides"; *vastae* (adj., nom. pl. f.) "vast," "huge," modifying *rupes*; *rupes* (noun, nom. pl. f.) "cliffs," "rocks," subject; *gemini* (adj., nom. pl. m.) "twin," "twofold," substantive used as subject; *minantur* (verb, 3rd pl. pres. indic. deponent) "threaten," "loom menacingly." The twin cliffs rise threateningly on both sides of the harbor entrance.
163:
**in caelum scopuli, quorum sub vertice late**

*scopuli* (nom. pl., "cliffs/crags") serve as subject; *in caelum* (acc., "into the sky") indicates their soaring height; *quorum* (gen. pl. relative pronoun, "of which") introduces a subordinate clause; *sub vertice* (abl. sg., "beneath the peak/summit") gives location; *late* (adverb, "widely") modifies what lies spread beneath. The cliffs tower skyward, and beneath their peak something extends broadly—likely the calm waters mentioned in the following line.

**aequora tuta silent; tum silvis scaena coruscis**

*aequora* (nom. pl. n., "waters/sea-surfaces") *tuta* (nom. pl. n., "safe/protected") *silent* (3rd pl. pres., "are silent/still"); *tum* (adv., "then/moreover"); *silvis* (abl. pl. f., "with woods/forests") *scaena* (nom. sg. f., "stage/backdrop/scene") *coruscis* (abl. pl. f., "shimmering/waving"). The protected waters lie calm and silent; then/above, a theatrical backdrop gleams with quivering forests.
165: **desuper** (adverb): "from above"; **horrenti** (present participle, ablative singular): "bristling, shaggy"; **atrum** (adjective, nominative/accusative singular neuter): "dark, black"; **nemus** (noun, nominative singular neuter): "grove, wood"; **imminet** (verb, 3rd person singular present): "overhangs, looms over"; **umbra** (noun, ablative singular): "with shade/shadow." A dark grove looms from above with bristling/shaggy shadow, continuing the description of the foreboding grotto setting.
166:
**Fronte sub adversa scopulis pendentibus antrum,**

*Fronte* (abl. sg. f., "frons"): "beneath the brow/face," indicating position. *adversa* (abl. sg. f., "adversus"): "opposite, facing." *scopulis pendentibus* (abl. pl. m./n., "scopulus" + pres. part. "pendeo"): "with hanging/overhanging rocks." *antrum* (nom. sg. n.): "cave, grotto," the subject. The line describes a cave beneath an opposing cliff-face with rocks hanging overhead, continuing the description of the nymphs' sacred grove.
167:
**intus aquae dulces vivoque sedilia saxo**

*intus* (adv.): "within, inside"; *aquae dulces* (nom. pl., f.): "fresh/sweet waters"; *vivo saxo* (abl. sg., n.): "from living/natural rock," ablative of material; *sedilia* (nom. pl., n.): "seats, benches." Inside the cave are fresh waters and seats formed from living rock, completing the description of the nymphs' grotto as a natural harbor requiring no artificial moorings.
168:
**nympharum domus: hic fessas non vincula navis**

*nympharum* (gen. pl. fem., "of the nymphs") modifies *domus* (nom. sg. fem., "home, dwelling"); *hic* (adv., "here"); *fessas* (acc. pl. fem., "weary, tired") modifies *navis* (acc. pl. fem., "ships"); *vincula* (nom. pl. neut., "chains, cables") serves as subject with *non* ("not") negating the understood verb. This describes the harbor as a home of nymphs where weary ships need no restraining cables.
169: **ulla** (nom. sg. neut., "any"), **tenent** (3rd pl. pres. act. indic. of *teneo*, "hold/restrain"), **unco** (abl. sg. masc./neut. of *uncus -a -um*, "hooked/curved"), **ancora** (nom. sg. fem., "anchor"), **morsu** (abl. sg. masc. of *morsus*, "bite/grip"). No chains hold the weary ships, nor does an anchor secure them with its hooked bite—the natural harbor requires no mooring equipment.
170: **Huc** (adverb) = "hither, to this place"; **septem** (indeclinable numeral adjective) = "seven," modifying *navibus*; **Aeneas** (nominative singular, proper noun) = "Aeneas," subject; **collectis** (perfect passive participle, ablative plural, modifying *navibus*) = "having been gathered/collected"; **navibus** (ablative plural, *navis*, -is f.) = "with ships," ablative of accompaniment; **omni** (ablative singular, *omnis*, -e*) = "from all," modifying an understood noun or used absolutely. Aeneas arrives at this place with seven ships gathered from the entire fleet.
171:
**ex numero subit; ac magno telluris amore**

*ex numero* – "from the (full) number/fleet"; ablative of separation. *subit* – 3rd sg. pres. indic. of *subeo*, "he approaches, comes to shore." *magno...amore* – ablative of manner, "with great love/desire." *telluris* – gen. sg. of *tellus*, "of the land/earth," objective genitive with *amore*. Aeneas arrives with seven ships salvaged from the total fleet, and his men disembark with great longing for solid ground.
172:
**egressi**: perfect participle of *egredior*, nominative plural masculine, "having disembarked" or "having gone out"
**optata**: perfect passive participle of *opto*, ablative singular feminine (modifying *harena*), "longed-for" or "desired"
**potiuntur**: present indicative, 3rd person plural deponent of *potior* (+ ablative), "take possession of" or "gain control of"
**Troes**: nominative plural, "the Trojans"
**harena**: ablative singular feminine, "sand" or "shore"

The Trojans, having disembarked, take possession of the longed-for shore, finally reaching land after their海上ordeal.
173:
**et sale tabentis artus in litore ponunt.**

*sale* (ablative of *sal*, m.) "with/in salt(water)"; *tabentis* (present participle accusative plural of *tabesco*) "wasting away, dripping, drenched"; *artus* (accusative plural of *artus*, m.) "limbs, bodies"; *litore* (ablative of *litus*, n.) "on the shore"; *ponunt* (3rd plural present active of *pono*) "they place, set down." The Trojans lay down their salt-soaked, exhausted limbs on the shore after landing.
174:
**Ac primum silici scintillam excudit Achates,**

*primum* (adv.) "first"; *silici* (noun, abl. sing. of *silex*) "from flint"; *scintillam* (noun, acc. sing.) "a spark"; *excudit* (verb, 3rd sing. perf. act.) "struck out"; *Achates* (proper noun, nom. sing.) "Achates" (Aeneas's faithful companion). Achates first strikes a spark from flint, initiating the fire-making process to dry and warm the storm-tossed survivors.
